name: Jane Kahn
life: “I still remember painting a portrait nobody wanted smiling.” People around Tideline Market know Jane by a small Sunday habit. Jane picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I volunteered to repaint her mouth until my child asked why she had to smile.
appearance: Jane has a loose dark braid, a small notch in the left eyebrow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a soft blue checked shirt. It usually goes with a thin silver ring worn on a cord. When somebody else has the floor, Jane gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in.
personality: Jane treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To leave the painted mouth until the figure's owner chooses.
family: Idris Marsh is Jane’s stepsibling. Jane picks the meeting place. Idris sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *A closing hour*, Idris says, “I wanted the party to be a surprise. The owner finally closed up because his daughter told him exactly what she wanted.”
connections: Carmen Daniels. They ask children what the face depicts before deciding how it ought to look.

reactions.situation: A visitor wants the painted figure made easier to recognize
reactions.response: Jane asks the original model which part has been misunderstood.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Jane lets the child choose whether to stand by the door or sit beside the window while another adult gets help.

reactions.situation: If a frightened person needs longer
reactions.response: Jane changes the plan openly and takes responsibility for the delay.
